name: patchutils
desc: Small collection of programs that operate on patch files
why: Operates on patch files as data, letting you split, filter and rewrite diffs, a neat look at what patches really are.

brief.what_it_is: Patchutils is a collection of about two dozen command-line programs that read, transform and rewrite patch (diff) files as data. Inputs are existing patch files; outputs are new patch files or listings. Tools cover combining two incremental patches into one (combinediff), generating an incremental patch between two patches (interdiff), filtering a patch by file wildcard (filterdiff), splitting a patch into one-file-per-patch pieces (splitdiff), and listing affected files (lsdiff). The executables list also includes gitdiff, gitshow, svndiff, patchview, move-to-front, and others.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage gives no separate mission statement. It describes the tools as fixing up real-world patches: correcting output from 'cvs diff', repairing hand-edited patches, and reviewing or merging pre-patches against the same source tree.
brief.how_it_works: The homepage does not explain internals. It describes each tool by its job: interdiff compares two patches against a common source, combinediff merges two incremental patches so each file is altered only once, and rediff compares an original patch with a hand-edited one to fix offsets and counts.
brief.install_notes: The homepage gives no install steps beyond the signed release tarballs at https://cyberelk.net/tim/data/patchutils/stable/ and a git repository on GitHub. No runtime, account, or configuration requirements are mentioned.
brief.standout: It treats a patch file as plain data you can split, merge, filter and repair, rather than something you only apply. Splitting one multi-patch file into single-file incremental patches, and merging incremental patches so each file appears once, are the less common operations.
brief.status: unknown. The homepage shows no release date, version number, or last-commit date. It does link to signed stable tarballs and a GitHub repository with an issues page for bug reports, so it is active enough to accept reports, but I could not confirm recency.
brief.caveats: The homepage does not list supported platforms, the license, or known limitations. The GitHub repository is mentioned but its URL is not given on the page, so I did not fetch it. The Homebrew description is a short one-liner and the homepage adds no detail beyond it.
quotes: Patchutils is a small collection of programs that operate on patch files.
Combinediff generates a single patch from two incremental patches, allowing you to merge patches together. The resulting patch file only alters each file once.
Report bugs using the GitHub issues page.
